title: Asymmetric MSS rewrite causing intermittent control-plane TCP stalls — postmortem and runbook
content:
Summary:
On 2026-12-10 we observed a pattern of transient control-plane TCP stalls affecting a subset of on-prem / private-VPC customers. Symptoms: control-plane Hello/heartbeat exchanges would pause for 20–90s then recover, causing short-lived routing churn and failing cached session reconstructions in customer firewalls. Impact was limited to customers with middleboxes performing MSS/MSS clamping or TCP option rewriting. Roughly 7 customers showed increased error rates and doubled control-plane reconnects during the incident window.

Detection & Monitoring:
- First alert: anomaly in control-plane telemetry at 2026-12-10T02:17Z — elevated keepalive retransmits and RTT variance for region-eu-onprem-1 pool.
- SRE pager triggered for network-errors > 0.5% across control-plane routes.
- Observability trails: trace spans showed large gaps between control-plane request start/finish; packet captures from collector nodes showed TCP segments arriving but acknowledgement stalls.

Initial Triage (timeline):
- 02:20 — SRE oncall collected tcpdump from two affected edge nodes and a healthy node for comparison.
- 02:35 — Noticed MSS values in SYN/SYN-ACK differing between directions (client->server seen with MSS=1460, server->client SYN-ACK with MSS rewritten to 1200 by upstream firewall).
- 03:05 — Reproduced symptom in lab with customer middlebox appliance (firmware v3.2.1) configured to clamp MSS and remove TCP timestamps; under this condition control-plane long-polling requests would stall during path MTU shifts.
- 03:30 — Rolled soft mitigation: reduced control-plane keepalive interval from 30s to 10s for affected pools and enabled aggressive retransmit backoff to reduce session hold-time. Immediate customer recovery observed within 2–5 minutes for most instances.

Root Cause Hypothesis (final):
1) Asymmetric path MTU/MSS rewriting by customer or transit middlebox produced directionally inconsistent MSS and TCP option sets.
2) Control-plane transport expects symmetric MSS and preserves long-lived TCP connections for KV/cache/longpoll channels. Asymmetric MSS combined with selective removal of Timestamps caused spurious retransmit timers and deadlocked kernel TCP stacks on our edge nodes.
3) Customer firewalls with aggressive session inspection occasionally rewrote sequence numbers / removed selective ACKs during reassembly windows leading to prolonged stall until kernel retransmit recovered.

Contributing factors:
- Our default control-plane longpoll and heartbeat keepalive intervals assumed stable path characteristics for private deployments.
- Edge TCP tuning (retransmit timers, SACK/timestamp dependencies) was tuned for cloud-friendly middleboxes, not for some on-prem appliances doing MSS clamping + option mangling.
- Lack of a defensive fallback in the control-plane to renegotiate transport (e.g., force reconnect over new socket when MSS/options mismatch detected).

Evidence snippets (sanitized):
- tcpdump filter: sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 'host 10.24.3.12 and tcp' -w /tmp/cp-20261210.pcap
- example SYNs:
  client->server: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 12345 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
  server->client SYN-ACK: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, options [mss 1200,sackOK]  <-- MSS rewritten; timestamps absent
- sysctl values we observed on edge nodes: net.ipv4.tcp_retries2=8, tcp_retries1=3, tcp_keepalive_time=30 (before mitigation)

Mitigation during incident:
- Short-term: lowered tcp_keepalive_time on affected pools to 10s and enabled faster retransmit (set tcp_retries1=2) via staged SSH+Ansible playbook to nodes in region-eu-onprem-1. This reduced effective stall duration.
- Recommended customer-facing mitigation: request customers to disable MSS-clamping for Redwood control-plane CIDR, or to upgrade middlebox firmware to vendor build that preserves TCP timestamps and MSS.

Permanent fixes / plan:
1) Control-plane transport change: add a proactive transport health detector that evaluates negotiated MSS/tcp-options on new sockets. If directional mismatch (MSS diff > 40 bytes or missing TS on one side) then perform a graceful reconnect over a fresh socket and mark flow as "option-mismatch" for telemetry. Target: Q1-2027.
2) Runbook updates (see below).
3) Edge kernel tuning: provide explicit safe defaults for on-prem regions (tcp_keepalive_time=10, tcp_retries1=2) but gated behind a customer opt-in and tested via dedicated canary nodes.
4) Documentation: onboarding checklist for private deployments to include middlebox checklist (MSS clamping, TCP option preservation, asymmetric NAT behaviors).

Runbook (draft): Immediate steps when customers report control-plane stalls:
- Step 0: Gather telemetry: list of affected customers, earliest symptom time, relevant collector IDs.
- Step 1: Collect packet captures: sudo tcpdump -nni <iface> host <customer-ip> and capture both directions for at least 60s.
- Step 2: Inspect SYN/SYN-ACK MSS and options: look for mismatches in MSS, missing Timestamps, absence of SACK or wscale.
- Step 3: If MSS mismatch or options mangled: repro on lab with customer's appliance (if available) or ask customer for middlebox config (MSS clamp value, packet inspection profiles).
- Step 4: Apply soft mitigation: reduce tcp_keepalive_time to 10s and tcp_retries1 to 2 on affected nodes (use ansible tag: cp-mss-softmitigate). Command example: sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=10; sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_retries1=2
- Step 5: If persistent, schedule controlled reconnect: drain affected control-plane connection using: curl -XPOST https://controlplane.local/admin/conn-drain?id=<conn-id> and monitor re-establish.
- Step 6: Engage customer: request disabling MSS-clamp for Redwood control-plane ranges or patching firmware.

Testing notes to dev/edge teams:
- Build unit test harness that simulates asymmetric MSS and missing timestamps to verify reconnect detector behavior.
- Add e2e staging test that runs control-plane longpoll under simulated middlebox with MSS rewrite and SSH-based automation to verify soft mitigation reduces stall windows.

Open action items (owners):
- SRE: create SRE-4521 (done) — implement canary sysctl changes and document safe rollback (owner: Maya Rivera).
- Network/Edge: design reconnect detector and small change to transport stack to inspect MSS/options on handshake (owner: Omar Kaplan). Target: 2027-01-31 for proposal, 2027-03-15 for rollout plan.
- Product/Onboarding: add a Private/VPC connectivity checklist to onboarding docs and include explicit middlebox guidance for MSS/TS (owner: Ravi Singh).

Post-incident notes / lessons learned:
- Long-lived TCP connections in on-prem environments interact poorly with opaque middleboxes; we need better defensive rekey/reconnect heuristics in the control-plane.
- Observability gap: we must capture handshake option telemetry (MSS/TS present) in metrics to surface customers that will be at risk before incidents occur.
- Communication: preemptive outreach to high-risk customers (older middlebox firmware, heavy packet inspection) could reduce incident recurrence.

Appendix:
- Example tcpdump extraction to show MSS: sudo tcpdump -n -r cp-20261210.pcap -tttt 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0' | egrep -i 'mss|ts|options'
- Kernel tweak playbook reference: playbooks/cp-tcp-softmitigate.yml (internal repo)
- Contact list: SRE oncall escalation matrix (page id: SRE-Oncall-2026)

If you spot gaps in the hypothesis or have lab reproductions with different middlebox behaviors, add notes here and tag owners. This doc should be the source of truth for the follow-up ticket SRE-4521.
